STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plate: the typical range is 20-30 cm. This one looks like a medium-sized square dinner plate, so about 23-25 cm.
b) Reference: the pineapple chunks are about 3-4 cm across. Across the plate width (~25 cm of visible plate) they fit roughly 6-7 lengths, which agrees with 23-25 cm.
Final width: 24 cm, so area = 24 x 24 = 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Pineapple chunks: 5 visible pieces, no hidden stack. Each chunk is about 3 x 2 x 1.5 cm, roughly 4-5 g... more precisely, a chunk of this size (about 9 ml) at 0.6 g/ml ≈ 6 g. Five chunks ≈ 30 g (the chunks are a bit larger than that, so I use 35 g).
- Scrambled egg: occupies roughly 15% of the plate area, about 86 cm². It is a mound about 1.5 cm thick on average (peak about 2.5-3 cm), so volume ≈ 86 x 1.5 = 130 ml. Density 0.8 g/ml gives about 104 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible; the plate is flat with nothing underneath. Small amounts only, so no additions.

STEP 5 - Energy:
- Pineapple, raw/chopped: about 50 kcal per 100 g.
- Scrambled egg (cooked, with some fat from cooking): about 150 kcal per 100 g.

Totals: pineapple 35 g → 18 kcal; scrambled egg 104 g → 156 kcal. Total about 139 g, about 174 kcal.
